companyDescription: Daily-refresh Earth imaging · Pelican/SuperDove constellations — the data layer under defence & intelligence AI, now growing 42% with D&I up 65%
priceNote: Live price Aug 13 07:49. Prior report (Aug 5) used $22.83 — +7.3% drift in 8 days, which is why this refresh was triggered. Stock is now 16.7% above the preferred entry band, so the setup is worse than the thesis.
summary: Planet's Q1 FY2027 was a genuine inflection: record revenue of $94.2M, up 42% YoY, driven by defence & intelligence contracts growing over 65%. That shifts the story from 'imagery subscriptions with slow growth' to 'defence data supplier with government budget behind it'. Consensus sits around $35.36 across 10 analysts (median $38 on a narrower 5-analyst set, range $22-$53) — roughly +44% from here. The catch is entry, not thesis: the stock has run 7.3% in eight days and now trades 16.7% above the $19-21 zone the last report set. Q2 FY2027 earnings on Sep 8 is the next test.

catalysts.name: Q2 FY2027 Earnings
catalysts.description: The print that has to confirm Q1 wasn't a one-off. Watch whether defence & intelligence holds anywhere near +65% growth and whether the Pelican Gen-2 ramp shows up in guidance rather than commentary.

catalysts.name: Pelican Gen-2 Fleet Buildout
catalysts.description: Higher-resolution Pelican satellites entering service raise revenue per customer without a matching cost step. Continuous rollout rather than a dated event — it shows up in margins, not headlines.

risks: Trading 16.7% above the preferred entry zone — the thesis is intact but this price gives up most of the near-term margin of safety
Analyst dispersion is wide ($22 low to $53 high), meaning the market has not agreed on what defence growth is worth
Defence & intelligence concentration cuts both ways — one budget cycle or contract non-renewal moves the growth rate materially
Still lossmaking; a 42% growth rate has to survive comparisons that get harder from here
PL fell 37% on a prior quarterly print (Jun 2026) — this name does not reward buying into earnings at the top of its range

estimateDates.note: D&I growth rate is the number that matters

macroRisk.rateOutlook: Fed funds 3.50-3.75%, held Jul 29 with three dissents favouring a hike. Next FOMC Sep 16, eight days after PL's earnings.
macroRisk.inflationNote: July CPI (Aug 12) headline 3.4% vs 3.5% prior, core 2.5%, +0.1% m/m — soft print, easing hike pressure after payrolls came in at -23k.
macroRisk.sectorImpact: MEDIUM rather than LOW: PL is an unprofitable long-duration growth name, so it carries rate sensitivity that a profitable defence supplier wouldn't. Offsetting that, its revenue base is government defence spending, which is far less rate-sensitive than commercial demand.
macroRisk.summary: MEDIUM — long-duration valuation risk, partly offset by a government-funded revenue base.
